reviewers.summary: The evaluator covers the stated state and UTC-window cases, but a partially resolved obligation can retain an outdated current draft.

findingList.message: Supersede drafts when new evidence makes their contents obsolete, even if the obligation remains AtRisk. Otherwise a current draft can still list requirements that are now satisfied, contrary to the acceptance criterion that new evidence makes obsolete drafts non-current while preserving history.

evidence.codePathTraced: Evaluate supersedes a current draft only when its basis differs or the obligation leaves AtRisk; it does not compare the draft with the current missing requirements.
evidence.failureScenario: A draft lists REQ-1 and REQ-2 as missing. New evidence satisfies REQ-1 while REQ-2 remains missing on the same basis and within the notice window. The obligation stays AtRisk, so the old draft remains Current with an outdated body, and no replacement is created.

reviewers.summary: The evaluator behavior is broadly covered, including precedence, current-basis review, UTC boundaries, and draft history. The no-send acceptance criterion lacks a test that would fail if recording a legal decision triggered delivery.

findingList.message: The legal-decision test does not verify the acceptance criterion that no notice is sent.

evidence.codePathTraced: Legal_sign_off_records_simulated_decision_without_changing_state calls RecordLegalDecision and checks the returned record and later obligation state, but does not observe any notification or sending boundary.
evidence.failureScenario: If RecordLegalDecision were changed to send a notice when recording a signed-off decision, these assertions could still pass, so the test would not fail when the required no-send behavior is removed.

reviewers.summary: No security vulnerability is reachable in the changed code. Legal decisions are recorded as simulated data; this code does not send notices or expose an authentication or authorization path.
